To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Darling–Eerdős theorem for sums with finite variance can be extended to multidimensional random variables, and (2) in a borderline situation, one has weak convergence of a shifted version of a standard limiting distribution in this setting.

the Darling–Eddos theorem for sums of independent random variables with finite variance holds for multidimensional random vectors with the same limiting distribution as for sums of one-dimensional random variables, but with a shift in the mean of the limiting distribution that depends on the dimension of the space and the covariance structure of the random vectors, and a new strong in-variance principle for sums of i.d.d. random vectors with finite variance.

(i) a new strong in-variance principle for sums of i. i. d. random vectors with mean zero and covariance matrix Σ is obtained, and (ii) this principle is used to prove an improved version of Darling–Erdös theorem for sums of such random vectors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions. What is the limiting distribution of a normalized sum of i.i.d random variables with mean 0 and variance 1 when the summands have a finite moment of order 1 + δ, where 0 < δ ≤ 1? What is the limiting behavior of the summands when δ = 1?

the following question: What can we say if we have a sequence of i.i.d random variables with zero mean, finite variance and a sum which is close to a constant multiple of the standard deviation of the sequence?
the study of the distribution of a random walk in a multidimensional setting, with applications to sums of independent random variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the multidimensional case, a Darling–Erdos theorem is valid in all cases except the borderline one.
the Darling–Eerdős theorem in the multidimensional setting is a very strong and powerful tool in the theory of large deviations.

in the multidimensional setting one has weak convergence in the Darling–Endős theorem to the standard limiting distribution if and only if one has convergence in distribution to the standard limiting distributions in the classical Darling-Erdős theorem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained an improved Darling–Erdos theorem for multidimensional random vectors and we have provided a complete characterization of the boundary case.
we have a new general Darling–Erdos theorem in Euclidean space.
we provide a new proof of the Darling–Erdoes theorem in the multidimensional setting and we provide a new strong incompressibility theorem for sums of independent random vectors with finite variance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the limiting distribution of a suitably rescaled sum of i.i.d.s is invariant under the group of linear transformations that preserve the covariance matrix of the random vector.
the limiting distributions in the Darling–Eerdős type theorems for sums of random vectors are not always Gaussian.
in many situations one may expect to see the same limiting behavior as in the one-dimensional case.
